teaches: A result: open on the outcome and the reason it happened; the preview is left out because it is not a result; two stories joined by what the second changed; the last line the most concrete name.

packet.title: Verstappen wins Singapore sprint after Russell crash
sentences: Max Verstappen won the Singapore sprint on Saturday, finishing two and a half seconds ahead of Lewis Hamilton.
Verstappen started from pole but was beaten off the line by George Russell.
Russell led into Turn One but ran wide over the kerb at the final corner of the opening lap and hit the inside wall.
The crash brought out the safety car and ended Russell's race.
Half the track was wet and half was drying at the start.
Verstappen managed his intermediate tyres from the restart with Hamilton and Charles Leclerc behind him.
Verstappen described his start as "horrendous" after the race.
Ticket sales for the weekend were the highest in the event's history.

packet.title: Norris and Piastri collide on final lap
sentences: Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri collided at Turn Five on the final lap of the sprint.
Norris drew alongside, Piastri held his line, and both cars spun.
Piastri hit the barrier and retired, while Norris fell to eighth.
The stewards called it a racing incident and gave no penalty.
Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes moved up to fourth after the collision.

packet.title: Sprint preview: Verstappen on pole
sentences: Verstappen is expected to convert pole into a win if the track stays dry.
Russell is tipped as the driver most likely to challenge at the start.
